# The Patternmaker Behind the Designer — complete editable platform copy

## 1. LONG VIDEO
Place sketch and finished dress at opposite ends, then refuse the jump cut. Walk through brief, block, pattern, toile, fitting, revision, grade, production file, and archive—with a named decision-maker at every supported step.

## 2. SHORT 01
“A pattern is geometry with consequences.” Show how one line changes balance, movement, material consumption, construction, and fit.

## 3. SHORT 02
“Do not credit the invisible specialist by guessing.” Find the record, ask the contributor, mark the unknown, and preserve the correction route.

## 4. CAROUSEL
THE SKETCH / THE BRIEF / THE BLOCK / THE FIRST PATTERN / THE TOILE / THE FIT / THE REVISION / THE GRADE / THE PRODUCTION FILE / THE CREDIT.

## 5. NEWSLETTER
Subject: Who made the sketch possible to wear? Use FIT’s patternmaking record to show skilled translation while keeping employment, ownership, and authorship claims case-specific.

## 6. FITTING ROOM EDITION
A live decision log with garment version, issue, wearer observation, proposed change, authority, approval, downstream effect, and archival note.

## Claim ledger
- **VERIFIED:** FIT describes patternmaking education as including draping, marker making, patternmaking, sample making, knowledge, craftsmanship, and technique. (S73)
- **VERIFIED:** The V&A records pattern cutting as material to the formation and practice of designers including Cristóbal Balenciaga and Alexander McQueen. (S74, S75)
- **INFERENCE:** A patternmaker translates design intention through skilled judgment; the precise authority, authorship, employment status, and credit must be established from the actual relationship and records. (S72, S73, S74, S75)
